extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, assignees, agents, and corporate IP staff submitting assignment/related documents to the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for preparing, submitting, and recording assignments and related documents (licenses, joint research agreements, arbitration notices, etc.) with the United States Patent and Trademark Office, including cover sheet content, submission methods, signature rules, and effects on continuations/divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet content requirements (37 CFR 3.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each assignment document submitted to the Office for recording must be accompanied by a cover sheet as required by 37 CFR 3.28. The cover sheet for patents or patent applications must contain: (A) The name of the party conveying the interest; (B) The name and address of the party receiving the interest; (C) A description of the interest conveyed or transaction to be recorded; (D) Each patent application number or patent number against which the document is to be recorded, or an indication that the document is filed together with a patent application; (E) The name and address of the party to whom correspondence concerning the request to record the document should be mailed; (F) The date the document was executed; and (G) The signature of the party submitting the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable descriptions of the interest include: assignment; security agreement; merger; change of name; license; foreclosure; lien; contract; joint research agreement. Cover sheets required by 37 CFR 3.28 seeking to record a governmental interest must also indicate that the document relates to a governmental interest and, if applicable, that the document to be recorded is not a document affecting title. A patent cover sheet may not refer to trademark applications or registrations. Form PTO-1595 may be used as the cover sheet for recording documents relating to patents and/or patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint research agreement cover sheet specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: If the document submitted for recordation is a joint research agreement or an excerpt thereof, the cover sheet must clearly identify the document as a 'joint research agreement' and must identify the date the joint research agreement was executed and the name(s) of the owner(s) of the application or patent and the name(s) of every other party(ies) to the joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using Form PTO-1595, identify the JRA in the space provided for the description of the interest conveyed and place owner(s) name(s) in the space provided for the party receiving the interest and other parties in the space for the party conveying the interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing address for mailed submissions (37 CFR 3.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents and cover sheets submitted by mail for recordation should be addressed to Mail Stop Assignment Recordation Services, Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313-1450, unless they are filed together with new applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for recording documents which accompany new applications should be addressed to the Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. Proper addressing helps ensure prompt and proper processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile submission rules and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments and other documents affecting title may be submitted to the Office via facsimile. Any assignment-related document for patent matters submitted by facsimile must include an identified application or patent number; one cover sheet to record a single transaction; and payment of the recordation fee by a credit card (use of form PTO-2038 required to keep card info separate) or a USPTO Deposit Account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The customer's fax machine must be on a dedicated line because recordation notices will be returned automatically to the sending fax number. The date of receipt is the date the complete transmission is received by the Office. If a document submitted by fax is determined not to be recordable, the entire document and associated cover sheet plus the Notice of Non-Recordation will be transmitted back by fax; corrected submissions must then be mailed to preserve the initial receipt date per 37 CFR 3.51. Documents that cannot be submitted by fax include: assignments filed concurrently with newly filed patent applications; documents with two or more cover sheets; requests for corrections to documents recorded previously; requests for 'at cost' recordation services; and resubmission of a non-recorded assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission (EFS/EPAS) content and fee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments and other documents affecting title may be submitted via the Office Electronic Filing System (EFS) or the Electronic Patent Assignment System (EPAS). Any assignment-related document submitted electronically must include: (A) an identified application or patent number; (B) one cover sheet to record a single transaction; and (C) payment of the recordation fee by credit card (use PTO-2038) or a USPTO Deposit Account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of receipt of an electronic submission is the date the complete transmission is received in the Office. If an electronically submitted document is determined not recordable, the entire document with its associated cover sheet and the Notice of Non-Recordation will be transmitted back to the sender; after correction the initial submission as amended may be resubmitted by mail to retain the initial receipt date under 37 CFR 3.51. Documents that cannot be submitted via EPAS include: assignments with newly filed patent applications; documents with two or more cover sheets; requests for corrections to previously recorded documents; resubmission of a non-recorded assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-signature and EFS character-coded signature rules (37 CFR 1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an assignment document or name change filed electronically, the person who signs the cover sheet may place a symbol comprised of letters, numbers, and/or punctuation marks between forward slash marks (e.g., /Thomas O’Malley III/) in the signature block (S-signature). An S-signature must consist only of letters or Arabic numerals or both, with appropriate spaces and commas, periods, apostrophes, or hyphens, and must be enclosed between single forward slash marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent practitioner signing pursuant to §§ 1.33(b)(1) or (b)(2) must supply his/her registration number as part of the S-signature or immediately below/adjacent to it. The signer’s name must be presented in printed or typed form preferably immediately below or adjacent to the S-signature and be reasonably specific to recognize the identity of the signer. EFS character-coded signatures must consist only of English letters and/or Arabic numerals with permitted punctuation and be enclosed in forward slashes (e.g., /Dr. James T. Jones, Jr./).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and sanctions related to signatures (37 CFR 1.4(d)(4) and §10.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: The presentation (signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating) of any paper by a party constitutes a certification under §10.18(b). A person submitting a document signed by another under S-signature or EFS signature must have a reasonable basis to believe the signature was actually inserted by that person and should retain evidence of authenticity. The person inserting a signature certifies that the signature appearing in the document is his or her own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of §10.18 may result in sanctions under §10.18(c) and disciplinary action for practitioners. Violations of certifications as to the signature of another or one’s own signature may result in sanctions under §10.18(c) and (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording date determination and returned-document resubmission (37 CFR 3.51)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of recording of a document is the date the document meeting the requirements for recording set forth in the regulations is filed in the Office. A document not complying with identification requirements of §3.21 will not be recorded. Documents missing other requirements (e.g., a completed cover sheet or required fee) will be returned for correction when a correspondence address is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned papers are stamped with the original date of receipt and accompanied by a letter indicating that if corrected and resubmitted within the specified time, the Office will consider the original date of filing as the date of recording. The period to resubmit is not extended. The procedures in §1.8 or §1.10 may be used for resubmissions to obtain the benefit of the USPS deposit date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior assignment on division and continuation applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a division or continuation application, a prior assignment recorded against the original application is applied (effective) to the division or continuation application because the assignment recorded against the original application gives the assignee rights to the subject matter common to both applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the assignment is effective as to the division/continuation, the Office’s assignment records will only reflect an assignment of the division/continuation if a request for recordation in compliance with 37 CFR 3.28, accompanied by the required fee, is filed. See 37 CFR 3.81 and MPEP §306.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments for substitute or continuation-in-part (CIP) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a substitute or continuation-in-part application, a prior assignment of the original application is not applied (effective) to the substitute or continuation-in-part application because the assignment recorded against the original application gives the assignee rights only to the subject matter common to both applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute or continuation-in-part applications require the recordation of a new assignment if they are to be issued to an assignee. See 37 CFR 3.81 and MPEP §306.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment effectiveness for applications claiming benefit of provisional application
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application claiming the earlier filing date of a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) includes only subject matter which formed a part of the provisional application, an assignment recorded against the provisional application will be effective in the later application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the later application includes subject matter not common with the provisional application, new assignment papers must be recorded for the later application, similar to continuations-in-part practice. See MPEP §306.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent issuance to assignee timing and procedural requirements (37 CFR 3.81)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may issue in the name of the assignee consistent with the application’s assignment where a request for such issuance is submitted with payment of the issue fee, provided the assignment has been previously recorded in the Office. If the assignment has not been previously recorded, the request must state that the document has been filed for recordation as set forth in §3.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for issuance to an assignee must be filed not later than the day the issue fee is paid. If submitted after the issue fee payment, the request must include a request for a certificate of correction under §1.323 (with the fee) and the processing fee under §1.17(i), and must state the assignment was submitted for recordation before issuance. For partial assignees and multiple assignees rules apply; only the first appearing name of an assignee will be printed on the patent where multiple names for the same party are identified on PTOL-85B. Assignment information printed on the patent is not updated after issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government license rights statement for contractor-owned inventions (35 U.S.C. 202(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Government contractor retains U.S. domestic patent rights, the contractor is obligated to include the following statement at the beginning of the application and any patents issued thereon: 'The U.S. Government has a paid-up license in this invention and the right in limited circumstances to require the patent owner to license others on reasonable terms as provided for by the terms of (contract No. or Grant No.) awarded by (Agency).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reference to prior copending applications is made in the specification’s early sentences, the Government License Rights statement should follow immediately as the second paragraph of the specification; if no reference is made, the statement should appear as the first paragraph. See 37 CFR 1.77 and MPEP §310.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing notice of arbitration awards and content (35 U.S.C. 294; 37 CFR 1.335)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an arbitrator makes an award concerning patent validity or infringement under 35 U.S.C. 294, the patentee, assignee or licensee must file written notice of the award in the Patent and Trademark Office for each patent involved. The notice must set forth patent number, names of the inventor and patent owner, names and addresses of the parties to the arbitration, and include a copy of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an award is modified by a court, the party requesting modification must file a notice of the modification with a copy of the court’s order. Any award is unenforceable until the required notice is filed. Notices should be directed to the Office of the Solicitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of licenses, security interests, and other non-assignment documents
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to assignments, documents affecting title to a patent or application (and certain other documents) will be recorded in the Assignment Division. Other documents not affecting title may be recorded at the Director’s discretion. Typical non-assignment documents accepted for recording include license agreements and agreements conveying a security interest to give third parties notice of equitable interests or matters relevant to ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A document returned unrecorded that the sender believes justifies recordation may be petitioned to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181. Recordation is not a determination of the effect of the document on chain of title; the Office will determine effect when ownership must be established for action on a patent or application. See MPEP §313–314.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing/cross-referencing additional patents against a recorded document
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to 'index' or 'cross-reference' additional patent or application numbers against a document previously recorded are no longer processed as informal indexing; such requests must comply with 37 CFR 3.11, 3.28, and 3.31 by submitting: (A) a copy of the original document (with reel/frame stamps or a copy of such papers); (B) a completed cover sheet; and (C) the appropriate recording fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will assign a new recording date to that submission, update the assignment database, and microfilm the cover sheet and document as part of the official record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment Division handling and examination process
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents and cover sheets submitted for recording are examined for formal requirements in the Assignment Division to separate recordable from non-recordable documents. Documents considered not recordable are returned to the sender with an explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the sender believes the document represents an unusual case justifying recordation, the sender may petition the Director under 37 CFR 1.181. After recording, documents and cover sheets are returned to the correspondence address showing the reel and frame number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reel and frame numbering and recordation stampings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent and Trademark Assignment System assigns reel and frame numbers and superimposes recordation stampings on processed and stored electronic images. Copies of all recorded documents will have the reel and frame numbers and recordation stampings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reel/frame identifiers appear on returned copies and are the official record locators for recorded assignment documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on USPTO officers and employees acquiring patents (35 U.S.C. 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers and employees of the Patent and Trademark Office shall be incapable, during the period of their appointments and for one year thereafter, of applying for a patent and of acquiring, directly or indirectly, except by inheritance or bequest, any patent or any right or interest in any patent issued or to be issued by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In patents applied for thereafter they shall not be entitled to any priority date earlier than one year after termination of their appointment. This statutory restriction limits filing and acquisition rights for PTO personnel.
